To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the turnover of proteins in different tissues varies greatly during development, but that there is a remarkable degree of coordination between the rates of protein synthesis and degradation.
the turnover characteristics of proteins change during development in a manner that is coordinated with protein accretion.

protein turnover is a major factor in the regulation of development, and that the degree of coordination between synthesis and degradation is a major determinant of the rate of change in protein concentration during development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of protein turnover in three types of development transition, namely, postnatal development, terminal differentiation, and perinatal development.
the regulation of protein turnover in the developing organism and in the adult organism in response to hormonal stimuli.
the regulation of protein synthesis and degradation in development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
protein turnover in development is not a uniform process.
the degree of coordination between synthesis and degradation is dependent upon the type of development transition.
protein synthesis and degradation are coordinated to varying extents in different tissues and during different developmental transitions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a high degree of coordination of protein synthesis and degradation, both between and within protein populations, in different types of developmental processes.
there is a high degree of coordination between the rates of protein synthesis and degradation in the three types of development transition studied.
the rate of synthesis and the rate of breakdown of specific protein populations are not always in balance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the coordination between protein synthesis, degradation and protein accretion is a dynamic process that is not only tissue- but also developmental stage-specific.
the rate of protein synthesis in a tissue or an organelle is not necessarily related to the rate of protein degradation.
protein synthesis and degradation are tightly coupled in the development of the three different types of transitions studied.
